icon.title: c@t
icon.description: An at-sign whose inner a is a cat: the a's bowl is the head, its counter is the face, the ears grow out of the top of the bowl and cross the ring, and the whiskers are cut in white across the sage. The ring keeps its gap and its tail, so it still reads as an @.

smallIcon.title: c@t mark, small
smallIcon.description: The same at-sign, with the whiskers dropped. Below about 32 px a 2.4-unit whisker is under a pixel and reads as dirt on the glyph rather than as a cat, so the small mark leaves them out instead of drawing them badly.

stickies.summary: Please be introduced to a cat
stickies.comment: Please be introduced to a cat who acquires things, for whatever purpose — maybe somebody knows.

**Content** is what somebody authors and a reader reads; **acquisition** is how
unstructured and semi-structured sources — documents, data, loose information —
get into the graph in the first place; **tools** are what an agent can call; and
**skills** are the instructions for doing the work.

All four are **declared directories** rather than conventions, so an instance
says which of them it holds and a consumer reads that declaration instead of
walking the tree.
